symptom: A microflow names another model element as TEXT (a Java action receives the string "Simulation.SIM_Tick"), so no reference exists for any checker to follow. Renaming or moving the named element passes Studio Pro, mxbuild and `mxcli check --references`, and the app fails at runtime — in the benchmark's app, the simulation stopped with an ERROR in the server log every second.
cause: Not a defect in mxcli: a gap in what any checker can see. Added lint rule MPR018, which scans the string LITERALS inside expression/value fields of flow actions and reports a literal that is exactly a qualified name of this project. Two design choices carry the precision: (1) literals, not whole expressions, because an expression's own references are also dotted ($Var/Mod.Assoc/Attr, Mod.Enum.Value) and those ARE real references Studio Pro renames — scanning expressions would report every association path in the project; (2) fields named Expression/Argument/Value only, found by reflection, because the sibling fields that hold references are named after what they reference (Parameter, Association, ListVariable, and JavaActionCallAction.JavaAction, MicroflowCall.Microflow) and reporting those would flag every call in the project.
insight: When a rule scans strings for model names, the dangerous direction is the one that looks safest. Reflection over ALL string fields is comprehensive and wrong — it cannot distinguish a literal from a reference field, so it reports every microflow call; an allowlist of field NAMES is the safe default because missing an expression field only costs a finding while missing a reference field invents one. The same asymmetry decides literals-versus-expressions. For the false-positive test, one check kills nearly all of it: require the dotted prefix to be a module the project actually has, which excludes prose, file paths, URLs, CSS selectors and Java packages (com.mendix.core.Core) without enumerating any of them. And measure precision on a corpus the rule can actually see: ctx.Microflows() is platform-filtered, so a run over testdata/pedapp mostly measures nothing — the 900-unit Studio Pro-authored submodule testdata/testapp is the real sample. Proving the premise took its own control: mxbuild reported 28 errors before the rename and 28 after, naming the renamed flow in neither, which is what establishes that no checker sees the text reference. `mxcli check <script> --references` is NOT that control — it checks a script against a project, so checking the rename script itself reports errors about the script and says nothing about the project.
